# ROS 1 bag fixtures

One small recording of a mobile manipulator (not a flight log): an arm's joint states, the base's
odometry and the transform tree, 17 messages, four connections, three chunks; see `make_rosbag1.py`.
Every file is generated by `make_rosbag1.py` and checked byte for byte by
`tests/unit/adapters/test_rosbag1_fixtures.py`. `oracle.json` is what the official `rosbags` reader
(fetched by `uv` for that run only, never a project dependency) reads from each bag, with
`uv run python tests/fixtures/rosbag1/make_rosbag1.py --oracle`: connections with their md5sums,
callerids and counts, and every message (topic, time, size, sha256), each deserialised by `rosbags`
to prove the payloads are whole. The adapter's tests compare their rows with it.

| File | What it is | What the adapter must do |
|---|---|---|
| `robot_none.bag` | uncompressed chunks, Index Data, Connection and Chunk Info records, Bag Header pointing at them | plan from the index alone; 17 rows |
| `robot_bz2.bag` | the same, bz2 chunks | the same rows |
| `robot_lz4.bag` | the same, lz4 chunks | the same rows |
| `unclosed.bag` | `index_pos` 0 and no index section, as `rosbag record` leaves a killed recorder's bag | `index_invalid` (info); scan; the same rows, no stated counts or extent |
| `empty.bag` | a closed bag with no connections and no chunks | a run and a clock, no streams |
| `truncated.bag` | `robot_none.bag` cut inside its last chunk | `index_invalid`, `chunk_truncated`; the whole messages of the cut chunk (the official reader refuses it) |
| `lying_chunk_info.bag` | chunk 0's Chunk Info counts one `/joint_states` message too few | `message_count_mismatch` (error); that message has no row |
| `unknown_compression.bag` | chunk 1 declares `zstd` | `unknown_compression`; chunks 0 and 2 land (the official reader refuses it) |
| `connection_collision.bag` | chunk 1 declares connection 0 again under another topic | `conflicting_declaration`; the index's declaration is read |
| `same_recording.mcap` | the same recording as MCAP (profile `ros1`, `ros1msg` schemas, `ros1` messages) | the acceptance test ingests it beside the bags and compares Run and Stream |

The compressed bytes depend on the pinned `lz4` and the interpreter's `bz2`; an upgrade may change
them (never what they decompress to), and then the files are regenerated. Tests also build hostile
bags at test time: cuts at many offsets, random byte flips, lying counts and positions, unlisted
and misplaced chunks, oversized headers, bz2/lz4 bombs, missing and non-UTF-8 connection fields,
repeated fields, a connection header of thousands of fields, unknown ops and top-level messages.
